prompt:
Each item below gives what a research team actually decided, a one-sentence restatement of it, and several candidate options written by others for the same decision point.

For each item answer:
- "faithful": "yes" if the restatement describes the same decision as what the team decided (abstracting away study-specific details is fine), "no" if it changes, drops the core of, or adds to the decision.
- "same": for each candidate label, "same" if the candidate is essentially the team's decision (a reader who knew what the team did would say the team took this option, or it contains the team's decision as a part), else "different".

Return only JSON: {"items": [{"key": str, "faithful": "yes" | "no", "same": {"<label>": "same" | "different"}}]}

ITEMS:

=== key f7ebf0ba9c51
What the team decided: When experiments failed, the recommended frame is for the mentor to focus on debugging why, e.g. training with better data or improving the prompts.
Restatement: Say the experiment did not work and steer the mentor toward debugging why, for example by training with better data or by improving the prompts given to the model.
C1: Steer the mentor toward diagnosing why the intervention failed, such as checking the metric and a positive control, before choosing any new intervention to try.
C2: Steer the mentor toward the next intervention to try, proposing two alternative approaches and asking which to run this week, rather than dwelling on the failure.

=== key 180cde3b60c8
What the team decided: Always include the prompt and show error bars (standard error heuristic, 95% CI = SE*1.96) so the mentor can rule out luck with small samples and critique the experiment.
Restatement: Always show the prompt and error bars, using standard error times one point nine six for a ninety-five percent confidence interval, alongside the experimental results.
C1: Show confidence intervals with sample counts for every reported metric, alongside a baseline run on identical prompts, on the same slide as the headline numbers.
C2: Show a handful of representative sampled transcripts next to the headline success rates and leave out error bars and extra baselines from the slides entirely.

=== key 3f5025980bd4
What the team decided: Prepare backup slides with a data-scaling plot (e.g. 1k vs 20k) to show that more data does not help.
Restatement: Prepare backup slides with a data-scaling plot comparing a small and a large training set size to show that adding more data does not fix the failed intervention.
C1: Prepare a positive control showing the measurement detects a known effect, plus checks that the intervention was actually applied, such as logged activations or outputs.
C2: Prepare a few sampled outputs from the intervened model and one hypothesis for the failure, and present them as the likely explanation without any further runs.

=== key aadc2545bd94

C2: Present only the two or three setups with the cleanest results, drop the exploratory and ambiguous ones entirely, and build the story around the strongest finding.
